tells: 1. Front row sits in near-identical listening poses (forearms on table, hands clasped at the candle), and the wide and held frames are almost the same apart from two people, so the row reads as parked mannequins (club-1-wide.png and club-6-held.png, front row of tables, centre)

2. The grey-jacket man folded face-down onto the table reads as asleep or drunk rather than laughing; with his head buried and his hand over his face it is the most obvious 'pulled out' moment (club-3-mid.png, centre-left table)

3. The laugh in the strip arrives as a hand-gesture swap more than a body event: no shoulder bounce, no head throw, no torso pitch until 12.8–13.0, and the purple-top woman stays completely static through all six frames (club-5-strip.png, right table, purple top)

4. The face close is waxy, with flat skin, a sideways gaze that doesn't land on the stage, and a stiff half-open mouth; the soft-focus heads behind are smeared and low-poly (club-4-face.png, centre face and left/right background heads)

5. The back of the house is a uniform field of dim, upright, identically posed silhouettes standing against the bar sign, and nobody back there moves or reacts (club-1-wide.png, upper half behind the tables)

1. In the wide, the rows stack like standing figures in a bleacher: second- and third-row bodies show full torsos above the front row's heads, the far-left figures look like they are standing or floating in the dark, and the lit block ends in hard edges against black side sections (theatre-1-wide.png, left third and rows 2–4 centre)

2. The front-row laugh is in sync: at 12.8 four or five people open their mouths together, with the same forward lean and hands on knees, so it reads as one triggered clip rather than a ripple (theatre-5-strip.png bottom row, and theatre-3-mid.png front row)
3. A stray textured sprite or hair-card fragment floats between the brown-hoodie woman's head and the man behind her (theatre-6-held.png, centre, around x=760 y=240)

4. Rigid hands-on-knees posture across the whole front row, the back-right man slumped head-down with his face hidden, and legs that seem to pass into the seat edges (theatre-3-mid.png, front row and right edge)

5. The face close shows plastic skin, a dark void inside the open mouth with flat teeth, and a spidery long-fingered hand near the chin that looks posed rather than reflexive (theatre-4-face.png, mouth and left hand)

1. Interpenetration: the green-tee woman's arm and shoulder pass into the dark-hoodie woman beside her as both lean in, and the hoodie woman's arm crosses into her neighbour (openmic-3-mid.png and openmic-6-held.png, centre pair; openmic-5-strip.png at 13.0)
2. The hair close-up shows hatched, stair-stepped hair cards with dithered alpha at the back of the head, very visible at 720p (openmic-4-face.png, upper right of the main head)

3. The wide's front row is a line of hands-on-knees, upright, near-identical seated poses with nobody turned, slouched or touching a drink, and two figures stand stiffly at the back by the door like placeholders (openmic-1-wide.png, front row and back-left by the door)

4. The laugh builds on the two women and the curly-haired man, but the yellow-shirt man and the man in the denim jacket stay frozen and expressionless across all six frames (openmic-5-strip.png, left half)

5. Faces at mid range are mannequin-smooth with the same smile shape, and the back rows have dead stares straight ahead with no blinks or head motion between frames (openmic-2-mid.png and openmic-6-held.png, back-row faces right of centre)
